claims.text: An operating system is the software that manages a computer's hardware and software resources and provides the interface through which users and programs use the machine.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Without an operating system, every program would have to drive the hardware itself, allocate its own memory and handle every device, so the OS does this once for all programs, from start-up to shut-down.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The operating system's key management tasks are memory management, file management, security management, hardware management (input, output and peripherals) and process management.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Memory management allocates areas of RAM to running processes and protects one process's memory from another, so programs run side by side without overwriting each other.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Process management decides which process runs when, so several programs share the processor, each proceeding as though it had the machine to itself.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: File management organises storage: it keeps the disk's directories and files, records where each file's parts sit, and controls access to them.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The operating system's own security management covers user accounts, access rights and passwords, deciding who may log on and what they may use.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Utility software supplied with the operating system maintains the computer: a disk formatter prepares a disk for use, a virus checker scans storage for malware, defragmentation software rearranges the parts of files so each file sits contiguously, disk analysis and repair software checks the disk's contents, file compression software makes files smaller, and back-up software copies files for safety.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Defragmentation moves the parts of each file together on the disk so the head travels less to read one file; the file size is unchanged, because data is moved, not removed.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A program library is a collection of pre-written, tested routines that a program can use, so software under development is often built from existing code.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Building from library files benefits the developer: the routines are already written and tested, so development is faster and the code is reliable; a Dynamic Link Library (DLL) is linked at run time and shared, so several programs share one copy instead of each carrying its own.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
